Beside the flow steps, ramb carries a toolbox used at every step —
track calculations, spatial tests, grids, timestamps, outlier capping.
These are the `rb_<verb>_<object>` functions. A tour with small
examples; the [reference index](../reference/index.html) has the full
list.

```{r}
library(ramb)
library(dplyr)
```

## Track calculations

Distances from [rb_calc_distance()](../reference/rb_calc_distance.html) are great-circle, in metres — on a
sphere by default, on the WGS84 ellipsoid (Karney's algorithm, via
[GeographicLib](https://geographiclib.sourceforge.io/),
[Karney 2013](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00190-012-0578-z)) with
`method = "geodesic"`:

```{r}
rb_calc_distance(-21.93, 64.15, -23.93, 65.65)
```

Speed from positions and timestamps, in knots (convert with
[rb_convert_speed()](../reference/rb_convert_speed.html) if you think in m/s):

```{r}
t <- as.POSIXct("2024-06-01 12:00", tz = "UTC") + c(0, 1800, 3600)
rb_calc_speed(lon = c(-22.0, -22.1, -22.2),
              lat = c(64.0, 64.05, 64.10),
              time = t)
```

[rb_calc_step_time()](../reference/rb_calc_step_time.html) and [rb_calc_duration()](../reference/rb_calc_duration.html) give elapsed times as
plain numerics in a chosen unit; the latter also works on lazy
[DuckDB](https://duckdb.org) tables, computed in the database.
[rb_number_runs()](../reference/rb_number_runs.html) numbers the runs of a vector — handy for turning a
behavioural label into stretches:

```{r}
rb_number_runs(c("steaming", "steaming", "fishing", "fishing", "steaming"))
```

## Interpolation

[rb_interpolate_track()](../reference/rb_interpolate_track.html) puts positions onto event timestamps — e.g. a
logger fix with unreliable coordinates — by linear interpolation within
a group (`by`), never extrapolating outside the track's time coverage.
On DuckDB tables it runs as an
[ASOF join](https://duckdb.org/docs/guides/sql_features/asof_join) in
SQL, nothing collected:

```{r}
track <- tibble(vid = 1, trip = 1,
                time = as.POSIXct("2024-06-01 00:00", tz = "UTC") + (0:4) * 3600,
                lon = seq(-22.0, -22.4, by = -0.1),
                lat = seq(64.0, 64.2, by = 0.05))
events <- tibble(vid = 1, trip = 1,
                 time = as.POSIXct("2024-06-01 00:30", tz = "UTC") + (0:2) * 3600)

rb_interpolate_track(events, track)
```

## Space and grids

Point-in-polygon tests come in three flavours —
[rb_detect_in_polygons()](../reference/rb_detect_in_polygons.html), [rb_keep_in_polygons()](../reference/rb_keep_in_polygons.html),
[rb_drop_in_polygons()](../reference/rb_drop_in_polygons.html) — and take
[sf](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) geometries:

```{r}
dansk <- rb_read_example("dansk") |> collect()
h <- rb_read_example("dansk_harbours") |> collect()
dansk_harbours <- sf::st_as_sfc(structure(h$geometry, class = "WKB"), crs = 4326)
dansk |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  mutate(in_harbour = rb_detect_in_polygons(geometry, dansk_harbours)) |>
  count(in_harbour)
```

The ICES statistical rectangle of a position:

```{r}
rb_encode_ices_rectangle(c(-10.5, 15.2), c(62.5, 54.9))
```

The default `method = "robust"` and `method = "vmstools"` (a faithful
reproduction of `vmstools::icesRectangle()` from
[vmstools](https://github.com/nielshintzen/vmstools), for compatibility
with vmstools-based workflows) diverge on exact 10-degree longitudes:

```{r}
rb_encode_ices_rectangle(-10, 62.5)                    # robust
rb_encode_ices_rectangle(-10, 62.5, method = "vmstools")
```

[rb_bin_midpoint()](../reference/rb_bin_midpoint.html) bins a coordinate to the midpoint of its cell —
here to 0.5-degree cells, then straight on to rectangles:

```{r}
dansk |>
  mutate(lon_bin = rb_bin_midpoint(lon, dx = 0.5),
         lat_bin = rb_bin_midpoint(lat, dx = 0.5),
         ices_rect = rb_encode_ices_rectangle(lon_bin, lat_bin)) |>
  count(ices_rect, sort = TRUE)
```

[rb_bin_midpoint()](../reference/rb_bin_midpoint.html) is exact for floating-point bin widths (`dx = 0.1`
places 0.3 in the 0.3-bin, not the 0.2-bin) and has a dbplyr SQL
translation, so it runs inside `mutate()` on DuckDB-backed tables,
including [duckdbfs::open_dataset()](https://cboettig.github.io/duckdbfs/reference/open_dataset.html)
parquet sources.

## Values and identifiers

[rb_cap_outliers()](../reference/rb_cap_outliers.html) caps a vector by one of three rules — `method`
again, not three functions:

```{r}
x <- c(rnorm(20, 3, 0.5), 25)
rb_cap_outliers(x, method = "miller") |> round(1)
```

[rb_add_timestamp()](../reference/rb_add_timestamp.html) adds a POSIXct column built from separate date and
time character columns, with explicit format and time zone:

```{r}
data.frame(date = "14/09/2025", clock = "15:30:00") |>
  rb_add_timestamp(date, clock)
```

And for AIS work, [rb_classify_mmsi()](../reference/rb_classify_mmsi.html) tells vessels from the other
nine-digit identities that show up in a feed
([MMSI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_Mobile_Service_Identity)),
and [rb_lookup_mmsi_country()](../reference/rb_lookup_mmsi_country.html) maps the MID part to a country:

```{r}
rb_classify_mmsi(c(251234567, 111251234, 992519999, 12345))
```
